extracted.intended_audience: Organizations and investigators preparing white papers or full proposals in response to ONR BAA N00014-23-S-B003 (prospective offerors for ONR contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, and other transaction agreements)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing and submitting white papers and full proposals to the Office of Naval Research under BAA N00014-23-S-B003, including technical, administrative, compliance, and formatting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated impact within the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated impact within the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the primary evaluation criterion (importance equally weighted with other top criteria). Assessors will consider how the proposed research would advance the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall facilities and capabilities of Principal Investigator and key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall facilities and capabilities of Principal Investigator and key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes assessment of: Offeror’s facilities — the extent to which the proposal reflects a coherent, coordinated collection of distributed facilities enabling focused, collaborative research, development, design, prototyping, pilot manufacturing, and workforce development; and qualifications, capabilities, and experience of the proposed PI, team leader, and key personnel critical to achieving proposal objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offeror's facilities (facility coherence and suitability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offeror’s facilities - extent to which the proposal reflects a coherent, coordinated collection of distributed facilities for R&D, prototyping, pilot manufacturing, and workforce development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators consider whether facilities support the technical objectives and collaboration needs. Facility descriptions should demonstrate capability and coordination across sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications and experience of PI and key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifications, capabilities, and experience of the proposed Principal Investigator (PI), team leader, and key personnel who are critical to achieving the proposal objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate relevant experience, complementary skills, and track record to perform the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall organizational structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall organizational structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation considers: suitability of the organization for performing the proposed work; academic and industrial partnership structure with well-defined royalty, licensing, and other revenue generation methods; effective mechanisms and policies to ensure robust participation by small and medium-sized businesses and by large enterprises; and well-structured and coherent Intellectual Property management across contractual R&D arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of organization for performing proposed work
rubrics_metrics.description: The suitability of the organization for performing the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address organizational capabilities, management structure, and how the organization enables successful execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership structure and technology transfer/revenue arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic and industrial partnership structure, with well-defined royalty, licensing, and other revenue generation methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe partnership agreements, IP/licensing plans, and how revenue or technology transfer will be managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small and medium-sized business participation mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective mechanisms and policies to ensure robust participation by small and medium-sized businesses, and by large enterprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain policies, outreach, and subcontracting/partnering approaches that maximize small business engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Property management
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-structured and coherent Intellectual Property management across the range of contractual research and development arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe IP ownership, licensing strategy, data rights, and management practices across prime/subaward relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential relevance to DoD and contribution to component mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential relevance to the Department of Defense (DoD) and contribution to a DoD component mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate clear alignment of proposed work to DoD needs and specific component mission objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of funds and proposed cost share
rubrics_metrics.description: The availability of funds, to include proposed cost share in the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For full proposals (not white papers), show realistic budgeting, funding sources, and any cost-sharing commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative importance of evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers: Criteria 1, 2, 3, and 4 are equally important. Full proposals: Criteria 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 are equally important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring guidance: indicates equal weighting among the enumerated primary criteria depending on submission type (white paper vs full proposal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and selection process transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will not be evaluated against each other since they are not submitted in accordance with a common work statement. ONR intends to review all proposals as soon as possible; recommended proposals are forwarded to Contracts and Grant Awards Management for cost analysis and responsibility determination. A recommendation does not guarantee award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that selection is based on stated evaluation criteria, administrative checks (cost analysis, responsibility), and availability of funds; notification of recommendation is not an authorization to begin work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced cybersecurity compliance prior to award (when applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Offerors may be required to demonstrate compliance, or the ability to comply, with enhanced cybersecurity requirements prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Appendix 2, Section F, Part 2, Administrative and National Policy Requirements paragraph (9) for details. Compliance may be a condition precedent to award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to small business participation (policy for contract awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of Naval Research is strongly committed to providing meaningful prime and subcontracting opportunities through its awards for small businesses and socio-economic categories (SDBs, WOSBs, HUBZone, VOSBs, SDVOSBs, HBCUs, MIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy informs subcontracting expectations and evaluation of subcontracting plans for contract awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting Plan requirement for contracts > $750,000
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed contract awards exceeding $750,000, large businesses and non-profits (including educational institutions) shall provide a Subcontracting Plan that contains all elements required by FAR 19.704 and FAR 52.219-9, as supplemented by DFARS 252.219-7003.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Plan must be attached to the Proposal Checklist and is not included in page counts. If the Offeror has a Master/Individual/Comprehensive Plan, include a copy. Plans are reviewed for adequacy; failure to negotiate an acceptable Plan may render the Offeror ineligible for award. Small businesses are exempt from this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting Plan goals and explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors shall propose realistic goals to ensure opportunities for small business participation to the maximum extent possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposed goals lack positive targets or SDB goals are below 5%, include a viable written explanation of why small businesses cannot be utilized and what attempts were made to involve them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices to Government-wide Point of Entry (GPE) for subcontract opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with FAR 5.206, certain contractors/subcontractors may transmit a notice to the GPE (sam.gov) to seek competition for subcontracts and increase small business participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices must describe: (a) the business opportunity; (b) any prequalification requirements; and (c) where to obtain technical data needed to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitating subcontracting arrangements and public posting
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR will post contact information of small businesses that indicate subcontracting interests and technological niche for prime contractor consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses interested in subcontracting should email the ONR Small Business Director with: Company name & website; Individual POC name & email; Business size & socio-economic category; Brief technology description (≤3 sentences, no marketing language); Technology keywords (≤10 words). Do not include proprietary information—submissions will be posted publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection and composition of evaluation panel
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers technical and cost proposals will be protected from unauthorized disclosure; the cognizant Program Officer and Government scientific experts will perform evaluations; support contractors may be used as subject-matter consultants but selection and award decisions rest with Government personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support contractors with access must sign the ONR NDA for Contractor Support, which contains third-party beneficiary language allowing direct action against contractor employees/employers if the NDA is violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export control compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors are responsible for ensuring compliance with all U.S. export control laws and regulations, including ITAR and EAR; proposals should address whether ITAR or EAR restrictions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must obtain any required licenses, approvals, or exemptions for exports of hardware, technical data, software (including deemed exports), or provision of technical assistance. Refer to ITAR/EAR texts and Export Control Reform Initiative guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security classification and classified access identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Government will attempt to enable work at the unclassified level; if access to classified material is required, the Offeror must clearly identify such need in the Proposal Checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If classified access is needed, a DD Form 254 will be attached to the award and FAR 52.204-2 will be incorporated. ONR does not provide classified access under grants or cooperative agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of animals in research (animal welfare compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD policies for the use of animals in DoD-supported research apply; Offerors must submit a Full Appendix or Abbreviated Appendix with supporting documentation (IACUC approval, approved protocol, USDA inspection report) prior to award if animals will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact ONR Animal Use Administrator for assistance and follow provided guidance links. Required documentation must be submitted prior to award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of human subjects in research (human subjects protections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must protect rights and welfare of human subjects and comply with the Common Rule (32 CFR part 219), DoDI 3216.02, SECNAVINST 3900.39E, 10 USC 980, and applicable FDA/state laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to award, submit IRB approval (protocol, consent document, IRB materials), proof of human research training, organization's Federalwide Assurance (FWA) and notification of suspensions/terminations; or documentation supporting claimed exemptions signed by IRB officials; or documentation that activities are not research involving human subjects. Documentation submitted to ONR HRPO via Program Officer; HRPO has final judgment. Awards will include a statement indicating HRPO review completion; research must not commence until HRPO approval notification is received. Government will not reimburse work performed in violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and biosecurity compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must comply with applicable provisions of DODM 6055.18 and standards at least meeting BMBL and NIH Guidelines, and any applicable FDA requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure biosafety practices and facilities meet minimum applicable standards; follow links and guidance specified in the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research involving recombinant (rDNA) or synthetic nucleic acid molecules
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must not begin performance of research within the scope of the NIH Guidelines until ONR has reviewed and accepted the Offeror’s documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a written institutional statement of compliance (on institutional letterhead by an institutional official other than the PI), evidence of IBC approval or determination exempt from NIH Guidelines, and DHHS letter of IBC approval or compliance. ONR review and acceptance must occur before performance begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Dual Use Research of Concern compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions and USG funding agencies subject to the USG Policy for Institutional Oversight of Life Sciences Dual Use Research of Concern must comply with all listed requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposal involves certain biological agents or toxins, contact the cognizant Technical POC and follow S3 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD High Performance Computing Program (HPCMP) access eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees of ONR instruments may be eligible to use HPCMP assets if ONR Program Officer approval is obtained and security/screening requirements are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If interested, consult HPCMP application and security requirements at https://www.hpc.mil/.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Review and Program Review Meetings (attendance and cost assumptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Review Meetings typically last ~one day (about 2 in-person per year); Program Review Meetings generally held once per year for 2–3 days; Offerors should assume 40% of review meetings will be at or near ONR Arlington and 60% at other facilities within the continental US.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include travel/meeting cost estimates accordingly. Offerors may propose hosting Program Review Meetings (include language provided), but inclusion of hosting language will not affect selection for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on procurement of foreign-made Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial Off The Shelf UAS may not be purchased pursuant to this grant/contract/prototype until a waiver per the Deputy Secretary of Defense memorandum is obtained by the cognizant ONR Program Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: waiver not required for unclassified campus research funded with Budget Activity 1 or 2 grants performed on campus; waiver required for efforts involving military personnel/DoD property/facilities, USG labs/UARCs/FFRDCs, PAO, classified, or exploring specific military utility; waiver required for all contract awards and other transaction agreements. Prospective performers must notify ONR Program Officer at submission or award changes and provide details; performers must cooperate to support waiver and cyber vulnerability assessment. No federal funding or purchase may occur until waiver and cyber vulnerability requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application formatting requirements (full proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Proposal Format: Spacing – Single-spaced; Font – Times New Roman, not smaller than 12 point; discuss technical proposal page limits with Program Officer; no page limitations to the Budget. Electronic file name must not exceed 68 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to these formatting rules; files must be PDF, no macros, not password protected. Non-compliant attachments will fail automated acceptance check and be rejected; resubmissions must be marked 'New' on SF-424 Block 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory SF-424 (R&R) family forms and specific field instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory SF-424 Research and Related forms must be completed as the cover page for all proposals; follow pop-up instructions and additional specific field guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow special instructions for fields such as Field 4a (Federal Identifier: use N00014 for new proposals), Field 4b (Agency Routing Number formatting), Field 11 (include ONR White Paper Tracking Number), Field 14/19 (email addresses used for EDA notification profile), Field 7 (Type of Applicant - indicate Minority Institution if applicable), Field 17 certification requirements, etc. Failure to provide required Program Officer Code identifier may result in rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project summary/abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The project summary/abstract must identify the research problem and objectives, technical approaches, anticipated outcome, and impact on DoD capabilities; use only standard QWERTY characters; spell out Greek letters; no graphics; one page or 4,000-character limit (whichever is less); must be marked 'Approved for Public Release'; do not include proprietary or confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts of funded projects will be posted publicly. Ensure abstract conforms to size/character restrictions and public release designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: R&R Other Project Information and Project Narrative attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Fields 1/1a (Human Subject Use), Fields 2/2a (Vertebrate Animal Use), Fields 4a–4d (Environmental Compliance) must be addressed; Field 8 Project Narrative must describe the research, objective and approach, keeping evaluation criteria in mind and be attached as a single PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the technical proposal as a single PDF to Field 8 (label as 'Technical Proposal'). The technical proposal must be organized into the required sections. Address NEPA/environmental impacts where relevant and consult technical POC for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover page required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical Proposal cover page must include: (a) BAA Number: N00014-23-S-B003; (b) Title of Proposal; (c) Identity of prime Offeror and complete list of subawards, if applicable; (d) Technical contact (name, address, phone/fax, email); (e) Administrative/business contact (name, address, phone/fax, email).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include exactly these items on the cover page; improper cover pages may complicate administration.
